record.original_question: Can one prove a cosmic no-hair theorem for generic inhomogeneous spacetimes, showing that sufficiently broad classes of expanding solutions with positive cosmological constant evolve asymptotically toward de Sitter-like behavior rather than relying on spatial homogeneity assumptions?

evidence.quote: Problem P12: Prove a cosmic no￰hair theorem in generic inhomogeneous spacetimes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth $4$-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g)\, g + \Lambda\, g = 8\pi\, T,$$
with positive cosmological constant $\Lambda > 0$ and a stress-energy tensor $T$ satisfying the dominant and strong energy conditions (with the standard modification allowing for $\Lambda$). The de Sitter spacetime is the maximally symmetric vacuum solution of these equations with $T \equiv 0$, and a future asymptotically de Sitter spacetime is one whose future causal geodesics are complete and along which the rescaled metric, curvature invariants, and expansion converge to those of de Sitter space.

Cosmic no-hair conjecture (generic inhomogeneous version). Identify a sufficiently broad class $\mathcal{C}$ of initial data sets $(\Sigma, h, K, \text{matter data})$ for the Einstein equations with $\Lambda > 0$ — not assumed to possess any continuous spatial symmetry and not assumed to be small perturbations of a fixed homogeneous background — such that every member of $\mathcal{C}$ which is initially expanding (i.e. $\mathrm{tr}_h K < 0$ everywhere on $\Sigma$, in the cosmological sign convention) gives rise to a future geodesically complete maximal globally hyperbolic development whose geometry is future asymptotically de Sitter in the above sense.

Equivalently: prove a cosmic no-hair theorem that does not rely on spatial homogeneity, isotropy, or symmetry assumptions on the initial data, establishing that generic expanding cosmological solutions of the Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant evolve toward de Sitter-like behavior in the far future.
artifact.status_search_result: The cosmic no-hair theorem has been established in numerous symmetric or near-homogeneous regimes (Wald's theorem for Bianchi models except type IX, Friedrich's nonlinear stability of de Sitter in vacuum, and various stability results for perturbations of FLRW with matter). However, a proof for genuinely generic inhomogeneous spacetimes with positive cosmological constant — without symmetry or small-perturbation assumptions — remains an open problem in mathematical general relativity, with only partial results under symmetry restrictions or for small data.

status_evidence.title: The cosmic no hair theorem (Hydrobates / A. Rendall)
status_evidence.snippet: To find a similar proof of stability for accelerating universes containing matter is currently an open problem. The proof used for the matter-free case is not easy to adapt to the new situation, and so far, a proof has only been found for certain cases with symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: Establishing the cosmic no-hair theorem beyond symmetric/perturbative settings remains open.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical Properties of Cosmological Models with Accelerated Expansion
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of rigorous results on accelerated expansion, noting cases with symmetry where cosmic no-hair has been proved and the lack of a general inhomogeneous result.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous cosmic no-hair results are restricted to symmetric or perturbative settings.

status_evidence.title: Cosmic no-hair theorem in homogeneous spacetimes. I. Bianchi models
status_evidence.snippet: Proves cosmic no-hair under Bianchi (spatial homogeneity) assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Known proofs depend on spatial homogeneity assumptions.
